question: An online store has: (A) the home and pricing pages, (B) 50 000 product pages whose prices change a few times a day, (C) the order history of the signed-in user, (D) a seller analytics dashboard behind login. Which mapping fits best?
options: A: SSR · B: SSR · C: SSR · D: SSR
A: SSG · B: ISR with on-demand revalidation · C: SSR · D: SPA
A: SPA · B: SSG rebuilt nightly · C: ISR · D: SSG
A: ISR · B: SPA · C: SSG · D: SSR
explanation: Shared static content → SSG; many shared pages with changing data → ISR; personal and current → SSR; interactive, no SEO, behind login → SPA.

question: A team moves its marketing site from a client-rendered SPA to SSG. Which metric should improve the most?
options: LCP, because the main content is already in the HTML served from a CDN
Server CPU per request, which goes up
INP only, because no JavaScript is needed
Nothing, SPAs and SSG have the same loading profile
explanation: The SPA must download, run and fetch before painting the content. Prebuilt HTML from a CDN gives a low TTFB and an early LCP.

question: An SSR news page has good LCP but taps on the menu feel ignored for a second on mid-range phones. What is the most likely cause and direction?
options: TTFB is too high; switch to a faster database
Hydrating the whole page blocks the main thread (poor INP); ship less JavaScript with islands or Server Components
The CDN is too far; add more regions
The HTML is too small; inline more CSS
explanation: SSR paints early but the page is not interactive until hydration finishes. Reducing the hydrated tree is what improves INP.

question: A developer reads the session cookie inside a product page that is statically generated and cached for every visitor, to show 'Hello, Ana'. What is the risk?
options: None, cookies are always read in the browser
The greeting of one user may be baked into the cached HTML served to everyone, or the route silently becomes dynamic
The page will not compile
The CDN will refuse to cache any page of the site
explanation: Shared caches and personal data do not mix. Keep the cached shell generic and load the greeting as a client or streamed fragment.

question: Which model ships JavaScript only for the interactive parts of a page while keeping one React tree?
options: SSG
Islands
React Server Components
MVC
explanation: Islands also limit JavaScript to interactive parts, but as separate roots. RSC keeps one tree and ships only Client Components.

question: When does a price change become visible in each model? Match: SSR, ISR (`revalidate: 300`), SSG, client-fetched SPA data.
options: SSR: next build · ISR: next request · SSG: immediately · SPA: never
SSR: next request · ISR: up to 5 minutes plus one request · SSG: next build · SPA: next fetch
All of them: immediately
SSR: after 5 minutes · ISR: next build · SSG: next request · SPA: next build
explanation: SSR renders per request, ISR serves stale until a request after expiry regenerates, SSG waits for a rebuild and the SPA shows whatever its next fetch returns.
